Is that proper grammar? Or should it be "leave the oven on?" Serious question

English, in its desire for structure as a bastard language, decided to borrow rules from Latin wholecloth. The thing with Latin is, though, that a lot of Latin "rules" just don't work the same in English. For example, the famous "split infinitive" would render a sentence gobbledegook in Latin but, in English, the phrase "To boldly go where no man has gone before" makes perfect sense.

OP's title uses the rule of never ending a sentence with a preposition (in this case the word "on") which is technically correct in the old-school world of English grammar, but which is more of an anachronism now than anything.

Welcome.

Be mindful that you have chosen a staged release distribution, meaning you will not have access to the latest and greatest software versions in the repos. For most people this is not an issue, but it gets annoying for some, if for example you know a certain kernel version has resolved an issue you are having, but the built-in tools do not offer it yet.

For instance, I had a read/write issue over USB3 ports when I first installed 17.3, because it was using an old kernel version which had a bug in it. Mint allowed me to install a newer kernel, but it was still out of date, compared to what rolling distros have on offer.

Still, this is a great starting point, and Mint has a great community behind it, so learn, have fun, explore and discover.
